_README: Corpus admissions (Sprint 40 P1; owner Decision 2 = A, OWNER_DECISION_BRIEF.md,
The candidate corpus is DERIVED: kpi_block.py, floor_tracker.py and
batch_parse select models by convexity.status in {verified_convex,
likely_convex}. So a licensed convexity run that writes a convex status
silently GROWS the corpus (Prep Task 6 measured 142 -> 143 on a scratch DB).
Decision 2 admits an in-scope NLP-gated model BY RULE: iff the licensed
verify_convexity.py classifies it verified_convex / likely_convex. Every
admission is listed here, by identity, so both denominators derive
mechanically and neither is a hand count:
kpi_block.py --corpus current     everything the DB classifies convex
kpi_block.py --corpus continuity  current MINUS the ids listed here
Headline KPIs are reported with BOTH, in one sentence (close rule C4).
The P3 application writer (apply_convexity_results.py --admit) is the only
path that may move a model into the convex set, and it takes its --admit
ids from this file. MINLP/MIP are never admitted: out of scope.

_admission_schema.classification: the licensed verifier's status: verified_convex | likely_convex
_admission_schema.license_edition: edition of the verifier run that classified it: licensed
_admission_schema.evidence: the verifier run, in one line, with its commit
